---
id: SA-0257
title: prepare_worktree's retry pause reaches time.sleep by module attribute, the shape its own suite treats as a defect
type: bug
priority: 3
estimated_lines: 49
estimate_measured: true
touches:
  - saffron/cell/worktree.py
  - tests/test_worktree.py
forbidden:
  - DESIGN.md
  - CONTEXT.md
  - CLAUDE.md
  - README.md
  - pyproject.toml
  - uv.lock
  - .saffron/**
  - .claude/**
  - ontology/**
  - tests/ontology/**
  - docs/**
  - images/**
  - harness/**
  - records/**
  - hooks/**
  - saffron/cli.py
  - saffron/task.py
  - saffron/batch.py
  - saffron/watch.py
  - saffron/events.py
  - saffron/ledger.py
  - saffron/report/**
  - saffron/record/**
  - saffron/gates/**
  - saffron/agents/**
  - saffron/repos/**
  - saffron/phases/**
  - saffron/cell/session.py
  - saffron/cell/runtime.py
  - tests/test_batch.py
  - tests/test_cli.py
  - tests/test_draft.py
  - tests/test_finish.py
  - tests/test_ledger.py
  - tests/test_ledger_fold_task.py
  - tests/test_package.py
  - tests/test_qualify.py
  - tests/test_reconcile.py
  - tests/test_report.py

  - tests/test_suite.py
  - tests/test_runtime.py
budget_usd: 8
max_attempts: 3
max_turns: 60
acceptance:
  - claim: >-
      `prepare_worktree` takes a `sleep: Callable[[float], None] =
      time.sleep` keyword, and its one retry pause calls that keyword
      rather than reaching `time.sleep` by the module attribute it calls
      directly today, at `time.sleep(_RETRY_PAUSE_S)`
      (saffron/cell/worktree.py:151). The same keyword, at the same
      default, already names this convention twice: `follow()`'s `sleep:
      Callable[[float], bool] = _sleep_and_continue` (saffron/watch.py:178)
      and `run_stack_batch()`'s `sleep: Callable[[float], None] =
      time.sleep` (saffron/batch.py:423). The witness overrides only that
      keyword, while a guard makes the real `time.sleep` raise if the
      pause ever reaches it some other way, following
      `tests/test_batch.py:294-303`'s own `_raise_on_real_sleep`.
    witness: tests/test_worktree.py::test_a_seed_whose_fetch_fails_once_is_retried_on_a_cleared_volume
    wrong_versions:
      - The keyword is added to the signature, but the retry's pause still calls `time.sleep(_RETRY_PAUSE_S)` directly, so the keyword is accepted and ignored.
      - The keyword is named `pause` rather than `sleep`, so this test's override, and the other witness's, pass it to a parameter neither call site reads.
  - claim: >-
      A seed whose fetch fails on both attempts still raises after exactly
      two seeds with one pause between them, and that pause also reaches
      the injected `sleep` keyword rather than the module attribute.
    witness: tests/test_worktree.py::test_a_seed_whose_fetch_fails_twice_raises_after_two_attempts
    preserves: true
  - claim: >-
      `prepare_worktree`'s `sleep` keyword defaults to the real
      `time.sleep`, not to `None`, matching the real defaults `follow()`
      and `run_stack_batch()` both carry at saffron/watch.py:178 and
      saffron/batch.py:423, so a caller that passes nothing still gets
      production timing rather than a silent no-op.
    witness: tests/test_worktree.py::test_prepare_worktree_s_sleep_keyword_defaults_to_the_real_clock
    wrong_versions:
      - The keyword defaults to `None`, and the function calls `time.sleep` only when it is `None`, so the signature's own default no longer shows the real clock the way `follow()`'s and `run_stack_batch()`'s own defaults do.
---

## Context

Finding filed against SA-0232's own head
(81246c7951cc6489a1c046d05caf4441f82f3303), where the retry this spec
touches first landed. SA-0237 then widened the seed's fetch refspec
(saffron/cell/worktree.py, between the `_seed_script` string and the
retry below it), so the line the finding names has since moved: the pause
sits at `saffron/cell/worktree.py:151` today, not line 146.

**The shape the finding names.** `time.sleep(_RETRY_PAUSE_S)`
(saffron/cell/worktree.py:151) is called through the module attribute
`time.sleep` rather than taken as an injected `sleep` parameter. Two
functions in this repository already take exactly that parameter, for
exactly the reason the finding states: `saffron/watch.py`'s `follow()`
takes `sleep: Callable[[float], bool] = _sleep_and_continue` at
saffron/watch.py:178, documented at saffron/watch.py:190-192 as
'injected rather than reaching `time.sleep` directly, so a test can drive
this loop to a deterministic end without waiting on a real clock'.
`saffron/batch.py`'s `run_stack_batch()` takes `sleep: Callable[[float],
None] = time.sleep` at saffron/batch.py:423. `tests/test_batch.py`'s
`_raise_on_real_sleep` (tests/test_batch.py:294-303) exists to catch a
build that reaches `time.sleep` by that module attribute instead of the
injected keyword, and is paired with an explicit `sleep=` override at
every one of its call sites (for example tests/test_batch.py:1949-1984).

**What `prepare_worktree` does today.** Two tests reach this exact pause:
`test_a_seed_whose_fetch_fails_once_is_retried_on_a_cleared_volume` and
`test_a_seed_whose_fetch_fails_twice_raises_after_two_attempts`
(tests/test_worktree.py). Both monkeypatch `worktree.time.sleep` itself
(tests/test_worktree.py:603 and :685 for the first, :685 for the
second's own copy before this spec), since `time.sleep` inside
`prepare_worktree` is read fresh from the module on every call, and that
is the only hook a module-attribute call leaves a test. A third test,
`test_a_seed_fetches_no_non_branch_ref_whatever_the_git_config_names`,
patches `worktree._RETRY_PAUSE_S` to `0.0` and `worktree.time.sleep` to a
no-op for the same reason, defensively, since its own claim has nothing
to do with the retry (tests/test_worktree.py:2596-2597).

**Why this is the shape the convention exists to prevent.** A parameter
default bound at `def` time (`sleep: Callable[[float], None] =
time.sleep`) captures the real `time.sleep` once, when the module loads,
before any test's `monkeypatch.setattr(worktree.time, "sleep", ...)` can
run. `saffron/batch.py` and `saffron/watch.py` both solve this the same
way: every test that cares passes `sleep=` explicitly
(tests/test_batch.py:1984, :2047, :2085, and dozens more). Nothing today
stops a future witness on `saffron/cell/worktree.py` from being written
against the module-attribute pattern instead, the way the two tests above
already are, and forgetting to patch it sleeps 60 real seconds.

## Problem

Give `prepare_worktree` the same `sleep` keyword `follow()` and
`run_stack_batch()` already carry, defaulting to the real `time.sleep`,
and read the retry's one pause through it instead of through the module
attribute. No caller passes it today, and none needs to: the default
reproduces today's behavior exactly. Update the three tests that reach
this pause to override `sleep=` explicitly, the way every `run_stack_batch`
call in `tests/test_batch.py` already does, instead of monkeypatching
`worktree.time.sleep`.

## Out of scope

- **A guard against the module-attribute pattern elsewhere in this
  file.** `_seed_script` and `_run_seed` call no `sleep` of their own.
  This spec changes the one call site the finding names.
- **The three callers.** `saffron/cell/session.py:1102`,
  `saffron/cell/session.py:1432` and `saffron/phases/package.py:541` each
  call `prepare_worktree` with no `sleep` keyword today, and a default
  that reproduces today's behavior means none of the three needs to
  change.
- **`_RETRY_PAUSE_S` itself.** Its value and its role in deciding what
  gets retried are unchanged. Only how the pause is invoked changes.
- **Any gate, hook or script outside `tests/test_worktree.py`.** No other
  file reaches `worktree.time.sleep` or `worktree._RETRY_PAUSE_S`
  (checked by a repo-wide search at this spec's base).

## Notes for the agent

**The three tests to touch.** Only
`test_a_seed_whose_fetch_fails_once_is_retried_on_a_cleared_volume`,
`test_a_seed_whose_fetch_fails_twice_raises_after_two_attempts` and
`test_a_seed_fetches_no_non_branch_ref_whatever_the_git_config_names`
reach `worktree.time.sleep` or `worktree._RETRY_PAUSE_S` today. Replace
each `monkeypatch.setattr(worktree.time, "sleep", ...)` and the
`_RETRY_PAUSE_S` patch with an explicit `sleep=` keyword passed into the
`prepare_worktree` call each test already makes. The first two tests
should also guard the real `time.sleep` with an `_raise_on_real_sleep`
helper, mirroring `tests/test_batch.py:294-303`, so a build that still
reaches the module attribute fails in milliseconds rather than pausing
for a real 60 seconds. The third test's claim is unrelated to the retry,
so a plain `sleep=lambda s: None` there is enough; it needs no guard and
no `_RETRY_PAUSE_S` patch once the pause itself cannot reach the real
clock without being told to.

**Where the new default lives.** Add `sleep` as the last keyword in
`prepare_worktree`'s signature (saffron/cell/worktree.py:94-108), after
`cap_add`, so every existing call by position or by the keywords it
already uses keeps working unchanged. Add `Callable` to the
`collections.abc` import already on saffron/cell/worktree.py:15.

**The comment, not the docstring.** `prepare_worktree`'s docstring is
already past ten lines (saffron/cell/worktree.py:109-131). Do not grow
it. A one- or two-line comment above the new parameter, stating why the
default is real and why a test overrides it, is enough, and keeps the
`prose` gate's `docstring-length` count where it is.

**No mutant on wording.** The comment's own sentences are new prose with
no fixed spelling to pin, so no `wrong_versions` entry targets its exact
words. The three listed above target the signature and the call site,
which are measurable.

**Measured.** A prototype of this change plus the three test edits ran
`uv run ruff format --check`, `uv run ruff check` and `uv run pytest -q
tests/test_worktree.py -m "not cell"` clean (54 passed, 9 deselected for
`cell`), on 2026-10-09. `git diff --numstat` measured 5+2 changed lines
in `saffron/cell/worktree.py` and 33+9 in `tests/test_worktree.py`, 49
total. `saffron/gates/core/size.py`'s own token count measured 167
changed tokens, well under the `bug` ceiling of 1300
(`saffron/gates/core/size.py:26`); `saffron/cell/**` is in `elevate_on`,
so size blocks at that ceiling regardless of this spec's own `risk`
field. Every wrong version listed above failed its criterion's witness
on that prototype: reverting the call site to `time.sleep(...)` directly
raised `AssertionError: real time.sleep called with 60.0` in the first
and second witnesses instead of pausing for real; renaming the parameter
to `pause` raised `TypeError: prepare_worktree() got an unexpected
keyword argument 'sleep'` in all three edited tests; and defaulting the
parameter to `None` with an `or time.sleep` fallback passed the first two
witnesses (both pass `sleep=` explicitly) but failed the third, which
reads `inspect.signature(worktree.prepare_worktree).parameters["sleep"].default`
directly.
